questions.question: What is the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 12 and 18?
questions.explanation: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6. The highest is 6.

questions.question: What is the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20... Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24... The smallest common multiple is 12.

questions.question: A number is between 30 and 50. It can be divided exactly by 8 and also by 6. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Find common multiples of 6 and 8. LCM of 6 and 8 is 24. Multiples of 24: 24, 48, 72... Between 30 and 50, the number is 48. Check: 48 ÷ 8 = 6, 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

questions.question: What is the HCF of 15 and 25?
questions.explanation: Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. Factors of 25: 1, 5, 25. Common factors: 1, 5. The highest is 5.

questions.question: Two bells ring at the same time. Bell A rings every 5 minutes. Bell B rings every 6 minutes. After how many minutes will they ring together again?
questions.explanation: Find the LCM of 5 and 6. 5 × 6 = 30 (since 5 and 6 have no common factors). So they ring together every 30 minutes.

questions.question: I am thinking of a number. When I divide it into groups of 5, I have 2 left over. When I divide it into groups of 6, I have 3 left over. What is the smallest possible number?
questions.explanation: The number has remainder 2 when ÷5, and remainder 3 when ÷6. Check options: 27 ÷ 5 = 5 R2, 27 ÷ 6 = 4 R3 ✓. 33 ÷ 5 = 6 R3 ✗. 27 is the smallest that fits both conditions.

questions.question: What is the LCM of 8 and 12?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40... Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48... The smallest common multiple is 24.

questions.question: A number is between 20 and 40. It is a common multiple of 3 and 4. What is the LARGEST such number?
questions.explanation: Common multiples of 3 and 4 are multiples of 12 (LCM of 3 and 4 is 12). Multiples of 12 between 20 and 40 are 24 and 36. The largest is 36.

questions.question: What is the HCF of 24 and 36?
questions.explanation: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The highest is 12.

questions.question: Ribbons come in two lengths: 18 cm and 24 cm. Jenny wants to cut them into equal pieces without any leftover. What is the greatest possible length of each piece?
questions.explanation: Find the HCF of 18 and 24. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Highest common factor is 6. So the greatest possible length is 6 cm.

questions.question: I am thinking of a number. When divided by 4, the remainder is 1. When divided by 5, the remainder is 2. The number is less than 30. What is the number?
What is the LCM of 5, 6, and 10?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30... Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30... Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30... The smallest common multiple is 30.

questions.question: Two numbers have an HCF of 4 and an LCM of 24. If one number is 8, what is the other number?
questions.explanation: HCF × LCM = Product of the two numbers. So 4 × 24 = 96. If one number is 8, the other is 96 ÷ 8 = 12.

questions.question: A number is between 50 and 70. It is a multiple of 7 and also a multiple of 3. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Common multiples of 3 and 7 are multiples of 21 (LCM of 3 and 7 is 21). Multiples of 21: 21, 42, 63, 84... Between 50 and 70, the number is 63.

questions.question: Students can be grouped into teams of 6 or teams of 8 with no students left out. What is the smallest possible number of students?
questions.explanation: Find the LCM of 6 and 8. LCM of 6 and 8 is 24. So the smallest number that can be divided exactly into groups of 6 or 8 is 24.
